confirmation: The owner checked the draft on a review page of 0.5 s edge frames and, on 2026-10-24, before any clip.py run on this video, answered: action ranges end at the last 0.5 s frame that shows the action; the whole Ammu-Nation visit is one never-pick range (heldout1); heldout1's action is three ranges split at the two Mission failed screens; heldout2's range starts at the skid (4:25.0); the Mission passed overlay is never-pick (heldout1). No range was corrected. The question whether the drives stay neutral got no separate answer; they are neutral as drafted. The owner then said to continue to the clip.py runs.
method: Drafted in PR 8, before any clip.py run on this video and after the final config was frozen (HELDOUT_PLAN.md, commit 6e0a9f3). Read by eye from ffmpeg frames only: one frame every 10 s, the whole video at 2.5 s, and every edge at 0.5 s (wanted stars on crops of the top-right corner). Every neutral stretch (0:00-0:53, 3:10-4:50, 14:10-14:49) was also swept at 1 s on crops of the top-right corner: no wanted stars, only the ammo counter. No clip.py, hudtest or other detector was run on the video.
note: Times are seconds in the source. Ranges are half-open (eval.py since PR 5): a clip that ends where a range starts shares 0 s with it. Anything in neither list (the drives with dialogue at 0:00-0:53.5, 3:10-4:50.5 and 14:09-14:50) is neutral. Every edge below was checked at 0.5 s; see each range's evidence. Not seen at 2.5 s: any phone call or pause map (one shorter than 2.5 s could have been missed).
rule: A never-pick range runs from the last gameplay frame before it to the first gameplay frame after it, sampled at 0.5 s, so it can only be too wide (revision 1 of test1/test2). An action range runs from the first 0.5 s frame that shows the action to the last 0.5 s frame that shows it (the start is revision 2's rule; the end rule was set by the owner in PR 8).
